content: 1. In the context of the HIV epidemic, a consolidated guideline has been developed to address the sexual and reproductive health and rights of women living with HIV. This guideline provides evidence-based recommendations to improve health outcomes and ensure the rights of these women are upheld. 2. A tool has been created to integrate gender considerations into HIV/AIDS programs within the health sector. This tool aims to enhance responsiveness to the specific needs of women, particularly in the context of HIV prevention and care. 3. Forsyth and Carey (1998) explored the challenges of measuring self-efficacy in the context of HIV risk reduction. Their research highlights the complexities of designing effective interventions and provides recommendations for future studies. 4. Empowerment, as a concept, has been extensively discussed in the context of poverty and health. It is defined as the process through which individuals gain control over their lives and make informed decisions, particularly in health-related matters. 5. Robinson et al. conducted a systematic review of interventions aimed at addressing unequal gender and power dynamics. Their findings emphasize the importance of improving self-efficacy and empowerment in sexual and reproductive health decision-making for women living with HIV. 6. The Mental Health Gap Action Programme (mhGAP) intervention guide provides strategies for managing mental, neurological, and substance use disorders in non-specialized health settings. This guide is particularly relevant for addressing the mental health needs of individuals living with HIV. 7. Guidelines have been established for the identification and management of substance use and substance use disorders during pregnancy. These guidelines aim to minimize risks to both the mother and the fetus. 8. Recommendations for couples' HIV testing and counseling, including the use of antiretroviral therapy for treatment and prevention in serodiscordant couples, have been developed to support a public health approach. 9. A guideline on HIV disclosure counseling for children up to 12 years of age provides a framework for addressing the unique challenges of disclosing HIV status to young individuals. 10. Maman and Medley reviewed the gender dimensions of HIV status disclosure to sexual partners. Their work identifies barriers, rates, and outcomes associated with disclosure, emphasizing the need for supportive interventions. 11. Smith, Rossetto, and Peterson conducted a meta-analysis on the disclosure of HIV-positive status, stigma, and social support. Their findings underscore the critical role of social support in mitigating stigma and improving health outcomes. 12. Medley et al. examined the rates, barriers, and outcomes of HIV serostatus disclosure among women in developing countries. Their research has significant implications for the prevention of mother-to-child transmission programs. 13. Kennedy et al. conducted a systematic review on safer disclosure of HIV serostatus for women experiencing or fearing violence. Their findings highlight the need for tailored interventions to protect women in vulnerable situations. 14. Colombini et al. explored the risks of partner violence following HIV status disclosure and the health service responses in Kenya. Their study provides valuable insights into the experiences of women attending reproductive health services. 15. Timberlake and Heywood provided guidance on encouraging beneficial disclosure of HIV status, ethical partner counseling, and appropriate use of HIV case reporting. Their work aims to promote transparency and ethical practices in HIV care. 16. The World Health Organization (WHO) has published global and regional estimates of violence against women, focusing on the prevalence and health effects of intimate partner violence and non-partner sexual violence. 17. Guidance on oral pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) for serodiscordant couples, men, and transgender women at high risk of HIV has been developed to inform demonstration projects and public health strategies. 18. A counseling tool has been created to support reproductive choices and family planning for people living with HIV. This tool aims to empower individuals to make informed decisions about their reproductive health. 19. Heffron et al. discussed key values to inform the design and delivery of services for HIV-affected women and couples attempting pregnancy in resource-constrained settings. Their work emphasizes the importance of ethical and patient-centered care. 20. The WHO has published medical eligibility criteria for contraceptive use, providing evidence-based recommendations to ensure safe and effective family planning options for all individuals. 21. Selected practice recommendations for contraceptive use have been updated to reflect the latest evidence and best practices in family planning. 22. The United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA), WHO, and UNAIDS issued a position statement on the use of condoms for the prevention of HIV, other sexually transmitted infections, and unintended pregnancies. 23. Specifications and guidelines for the procurement of male latex condoms have been established to ensure quality and safety standards are met. 24. The International Organization for Standardization (ISO) has published requirements and test methods for natural rubber latex male condoms, providing a framework for quality assurance. 25. The WHO has developed a medical eligibility criteria wheel for contraceptive use, offering a user-friendly tool for healthcare providers to guide family planning decisions. 26. A WHO statement on cesarean section rates provides evidence-based recommendations to ensure safe and appropriate use of this surgical intervention. 27. Kennedy et al. conducted a systematic review of the risks and benefits of elective cesarean sections for women living with HIV. Their findings inform clinical decision-making and patient counseling. 28. Bowser and Hill explored evidence of disrespect and abuse in facility-based childbirth, highlighting the need for respectful maternity care practices. 29. The WHO has published guidelines for the prevention and treatment of maternal peripartum infections, providing evidence-based recommendations to improve maternal health outcomes. 30. A consolidated guideline on sexual and reproductive health and rights of women living with HIV has been developed to address the unique challenges faced by this population. 31. WHO recommendations for the prevention and treatment of postpartum hemorrhage provide a comprehensive framework for managing this life-threatening condition. 32. Updates on HIV and infant feeding practices emphasize the duration of breastfeeding and the role of health services in supporting mothers living with HIV. 33. WHO recommendations for the augmentation of labor provide evidence-based guidance to ensure safe and effective management of childbirth. 34. Global guidance on the elimination of mother-to-child transmission of HIV and syphilis outlines criteria and processes for validation. 35. Male involvement in the prevention of mother-to-child transmission of HIV is emphasized as a critical component of comprehensive care. 36. A toolkit for expanding and simplifying treatment for pregnant women living with HIV provides practical guidance for managing the transition to Option B/B+. 37. A clinical practice handbook for safe abortion offers evidence-based recommendations to ensure safe and accessible abortion care. 38. Health worker roles in safe abortion care and post-abortion contraception are outlined to support the delivery of comprehensive reproductive health services. 39. Manski et al. reviewed the integration of abortion and HIV care, highlighting the need for evidence-based approaches to address the unique needs of women living with HIV. 40. Saleem et al. conducted a systematic review of medical and surgical abortion for women living with HIV, providing critical insights into the safety and efficacy of these procedures. 41. WHO guidelines for the management of sexually transmitted infections provide a comprehensive framework for diagnosis, treatment, and prevention. 42. A guide to essential practices for managing sexually transmitted and other reproductive tract infections has been developed to support healthcare providers. 43. WHO guidelines for the treatment of Chlamydia trachomatis, Treponema pallidum (syphilis), Neisseria gonorrhoeae, and genital herpes simplex virus provide evidence-based recommendations for managing these infections. 44. The WHO position paper on human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccines outlines recommendations for the prevention of cervical cancer. 45. Comprehensive cervical cancer control guidelines provide essential practices for prevention, screening, and treatment. 46. A framework for integrating gender into HIV/AIDS programs emphasizes the importance of addressing gender disparities in health outcomes. 47. The WHO global strategy on people-centered and integrated health services highlights the need for holistic and patient-centered approaches to healthcare delivery. 48. A framework for linking sexual and reproductive health and HIV/AIDS services provides practical guidance for program planners and healthcare providers. 49. The Inter-Agency Task Team (IATT) on the Prevention and Treatment of HIV in Pregnant Women, Mothers, and Children has developed a monitoring and evaluation framework for antiretroviral treatment programs. 50. A tool for strengthening gender-sensitive national HIV and sexual and reproductive health monitoring and evaluation systems has been created to support data-driven decision-making.
